summary:
[  edit  ]
The Video Device In  TOP  can be used to capture video from an external camera, capture card, capture dongle, IP camera, or video decoder connected to the system. Multiple devices can simultaneously stream video into TouchDesigner by using multiple Device In TOPs. HD-SDI video can be streamed into TouchDesigner through capture cards such and those from  Blackmagic Design ,  AJA  and  Deltacast .
If the device does not seem to provide a video stream but it is visible in the  Cameras  parameter menu, make sure no other applications are currently using the device.
TIP : Create an  Info DAT  and point it to the Video Device In  TOP  to see what devices are currently attached. The  Info CHOP  gives data for analyzing the performance of Video Device In and Out TOPs. Additionally, the  Info CHOP  can be used to obtain timecode embeded into the source signal on some device, as indicated in the below list.
Major capture devices vendors currently supported:
Blackmagic Design 	- Supports Timecode. Windows and macOS.
AJA  - Supports Timecode. Windows only and macOS.
Deltacast 	- Supports Timecode. Windows only.
Bluefish444  - Supports Timecode. Windows only.
Also supported with native drivers are some models from Datapath SDI, Allied Vision, Imaging Development Systems (IDS), FLIR/Point Grey, and Ximea.
AJA and Blackmagic Design devices support 12-bit input and output formats, including AJA’s ability to capture at a full 12-bit RGB 4:4:4.
For Magewell HDMI-to-USB3 capture (highly recommended, no drivers, plug-and-play), see  Magewell .
IP Cameras and USB3  include models from:
Allied Vision  - PvAPI SDK models only, not Vimba SDK.  Prosilica Series and Manta cameras. Windows only.
Point Grey FLIR Flycapture2 and Spinnaker  - Windows only.
Imaging Development Systems (IDS)  - TouchDesigner implements both the  uEye IDS Software Suite  and the 'Peak' SDKs.  GigE Vision  cameras are currently not supported.
Ximea  - Windows only.
Only a small subset of cameras from each manufacturer has been tested in-house, however it's expected that any modern camera from the supported manufacturer should work. If any issues are encountered please contact  support@derivative.ca .
See also  Video Device Out TOP .

parameters.label: Deinterlace
parameters.name: deinterlace
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets which fields to show.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Shows the entire frame as one image without any deinterlacing.

parameters.label: Even
parameters.name: even
parameters.description: Shows Even fields only. Line 1 is the top line of the frame. This will show lines 2, 4, 6, 8 etc, starting at the second from top line, and ending at the very bottom line.

parameters.label: Odd
parameters.name: odd
parameters.description: Shows Odd fields only. Line 1 is the top line of the frame, so this will show lines 1, 3, 5, 7 etc, starting at the very top line.

parameters.label: Bob (Split)
parameters.name: bob
parameters.description: Alternatively shows the even then odd fields, resulting in twice the framerate being shown, and removing the interlacing artifacts. Which field is shown first is controlled by the 'Field Precedence' parameter.

parameters.label: Field Precedence
parameters.name: precedence
parameters.description: ⊞  - When using Bob (Split) deinterlacing, this selects which field is shown first for each frame.

parameters.label: Even
parameters.name: even
parameters.description: Shows the Even lines first, then the Odd ones. Line 1 is the top line of the frame. This will show lines 2, 4, 6, 8 etc first, then the next cook it will shows lines 1, 3, 5, 7 etc.

parameters.label: Odd
parameters.name: odd
parameters.description: Shows the Odd lines first, then the  Event  ones. Line 1 is the top line of the frame. This will show lines 1, 3, 5, 7 etc first, then the next cook it will shows lines 2, 4, 6, 8 etc.

parameters.label: TV  Channel

parameters.label: Signal Format

parameters.description: The signal format to capture input at. This is the resolution and the frame rate, as well as if the frames are progressive or interlaced. Note that when using an interlaced format, the rate refers to fields per second.

parameters.label: Quad  Link
parameters.name: quadlink
parameters.description: Used for cards that support quad-link formats. Quad-link esstenially takes 4 inputs and creates one single larger input out of them, for example 4 1080p inputs become a single 4K input.

parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.name: acescg

parameters.label: ACESproxy
parameters.name: acesproxy
parameters.description: ACESproxy  color space, which has a log transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Input  Reference  White
parameters.name: inputreferencewhite
parameters.description: ⊞  - When converting the input color values to the Working Color Space, this controls how they should be treated with respect to  Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same  Reference  White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the  Reference  White level (brightness) of the colors will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR  Reference  White of 120 nits, and the HDR  Reference  White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR  Reference  White, based on the color space detected/selected.

parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.name: sdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Input Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.name: hdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Input Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: Transfer Mode
parameters.name: transfermode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how the frames are transferred from the input device to CPU memory, and how they are transferred from CPU memory to the  GPU .

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: automatic
parameters.description: Will choose the best transfer mode for the components installed on the computer. In general this will be 'Pre-Upload'.

parameters.label: Pre-Upload
parameters.name: preupload
parameters.description: Upload the frames to the  GPU  as they arrived. This ensures the data is already in  GPU  memory when the  GPU  wants to process it.

parameters.label: On-Demand
parameters.name: ondemand
parameters.description: Only upload frames to the  GPU  if the  TOP  is going to display them for that cook. This reduces PCIe bandwidth between the  GPU  and CPU memory in cases where the  TOP  is showing less frames than what the input device is capturing. However this means the  GPU  may stall waiting for that frame to be uploaded.

parameters.label: On-Demand, Sync to Frame Input
parameters.name: ondemandsync
parameters.description: This mode is currently only available for  AJA  devices. This causes the whole TouchDesigner process to stall until right after a frame arrives on this input. Then the process will start executing and use that input frame for this nodes cook. This removes any latency from the capture input, but can result in worse performance. Real-time should turned off for the TouchDesigner process at the top of the UI, and only one node should be set to this mode in a single process.

parameters.label: Memory Mode
parameters.name: memorymode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls the memory type used to transfer data between the capture card and the  GPU .

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: automatic
parameters.description: Will choose the best memory mode for the transfer. This will be 'Pinned' for capture cards that support it, and 'Regular' if not.

parameters.label: Pinned
parameters.name: pinned
parameters.description: Pinned memory allows data to be transferred in 2 copies instead of three. Capture->Pinned CPU Memory, Pinned CPU Memory-> GPU  Memory.

parameters.label: Regular
parameters.name: regular
parameters.description: The regular memory mode means 3 copies are required. Capture->Capture Writable Memory, Capture Writable Memory-> GPU  Readable Memory,  GPU  Readable Memory-> GPU  Memory.

parameters.label: Sync Inputs
parameters.name: syncinputs
parameters.description: Enabling syncing of multiple Video Device In TOPs. Syncing allows multiple nodes using multiple inputs and capture cards on a single system to ensure they are outputting frames in sync. Without this each node will be free running and will possible be outputting frames that came it at different times due to internal queuing. It's important the input sources are GenLocked to ensure all of their data arrives to all of the inputs at the same time, otherwise syncing will not work. This feature is currently supported for Blackmagic, DataPath, Deltacast and BlueFish devices.

parameters.label: Sync  Group  Index
parameters.name: syncgroupindex
parameters.description: There can be multiple sync groups active in a  .toe  file. Nodes will only sync to other nodes that are part of the same sync group.

parameters.label: Max Sync Offset (ms)
parameters.name: maxsyncoffset
parameters.description: Specified in milliseconds. The maximum difference in time two image could have arrived at be considered in-sync. Images that arrive at times more different than this offset will be considered to be part of different 'frame'.

parameters.label: Sync Timeout (ms)
parameters.name: synctimeout
parameters.description: How much time to wait for all frames in a sync group to become available before giving up trying to sync. Expressed in milliseconds. If this timeout elapses when waiting for a frame from one or more sources in the sync group, all of the nodes in the sync group will keep their current image and not output a new image, even if some new images arrived on some of the inputs.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution

parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the  GLSL TOP  when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected  TOP 's image.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does  not  apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to  sRGB .

parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.name: acescg
parameters.description: ACEScg  (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.description: ⊞  - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to  Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same  Reference  White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the  Reference  White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR  Reference  White of 120 nits, and the HDR  Reference  White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR  Reference  White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.name: useparent
parameters.description: Will use the  Reference  White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use  Parent ' selected, then 'UI  Reference  White' will be used.

parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.name: sdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.name: hdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: UI
parameters.name: ui
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI  Reference  White Nits' value for it's brightness.

parameters.label: connected
parameters.description: 1 if the node is successfully connected to the device, 0 if not. This does not necessarily mean there is valid input coming to the device.

parameters.label: sync_timeouts
parameters.description: When using the 'Sync  Group ' feature, this counts how many times the group failed to all provide a frame with similar enough timestamps within the timeout period.

parameters.label: last_sync_wait
parameters.description: How long the node had to wait from the time it was ready for a new frame until all the inputs provided valid frames for a synced output.

parameters.label: odd_field
parameters.description: When de-interlacing an interlaced input, this will be 1 when the odd field is being shown and 0 when the even field is being shown.

parameters.label: capture_fps
parameters.description: The calculated number of frames per second that are being captured by the device. This does  not  map directly to the signal format rate. It won't show 59.97 for example. This is simply a count of how many frames were captured in the last 1000ms.

parameters.label: capture_total
parameters.description: The total number of frames that have been captured this capture began.

parameters.label: frames_repeated
parameters.description: How many times the node has shown the same frame more than once. It does not currently correct for if the repeats are expected, such as when capturing a 30hz signal but TouchDesigner is running at 60fps. In that case the channel will keep increasing since each captured frame will be shown twice.

parameters.label: frames_dropped
parameters.description: This counts how many frames were captured by the card, but never consumed by TouchDesigner's reading thread. This occurs if the capture is running faster than TouchDesigner is able to consume frames.

parameters.label: frames_skipped
parameters.description: This counts how many frames were consumed by TouchDesigner's reading thread, but never consumed by the node itself. This can occur if TouchDesigner isn't running at full frame rate.

parameters.label: connection_changes
parameters.description: Counts connection changes, not supported by all devices.

parameters.label: temperature
parameters.description: On supported devices, outputs the temperature of the device in celsius. Will be a very negative number for devices that don't support it.

parameters.label: signal_fps
parameters.description: The actual signal format  FPS  of the input signal. 0 if unknown.

parameters.label: rgb_input
parameters.description: Will be 1 if the input is detected as an RGB (such as RGB 4:4:4) format. 0 if it is a YUV/YCbCr based. -1 if it is unknown or not supported by the the library.

parameters.label: frame_queue_length
parameters.description: The number of receieved frames queued inside TouchDesigner.

parameters.label: frame_hw_queue_length
parameters.description: The number of frames still queued on the device that TouchDesigner has not yet read.

parameters.label: last_dma_copy_time
parameters.description: The number of milliseconds it took to copy the last frame from the device to the CPU. -1 if this is not measured.

parameters.label: frame_timestamp
parameters.description: Time in seconds of the last frame displayed. -1 if this is not provided by the device.

parameters.label: resx
parameters.description: Horizontal resolution of the  TOP  in pixels.

parameters.label: resy
parameters.description: Vertical resolution of the  TOP  in pixels.

parameters.label: aspectx
parameters.description: Horizontal aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: aspecty
parameters.description: Vertical aspect of the  TOP .

parameters.label: depth
parameters.description: Depth of 2D or 3D array if this  TOP  contains a 2D or 3D texture array.

parameters.label: gpu_memory_used
parameters.description: Total amount of texture memory used by this  TOP .

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.
